claude_only.name: Which identifier is the authoritative, immutable handle for this plan, and which system issued it?
What distinguishes this plan from the adjacent plans, tasks and projects it references?
What planning horizon and time granularity does the plan claim to cover?
Which planned actions and schedule entries are constituent parts rather than merely referenced?
What degree of authority does this plan assert: proposal, plan, directive or order?
Which plan kind applies, such as project schedule, operational routine, agent action plan or service plan?
Which parties may act on this plan without a further approval step?
On what scale is priority or urgency expressed, and what does each level oblige?
Which changes require the revision counter to increment, and which do not?
When two replicas hold the same plan identifier, which revision wins and by what tiebreak?
How is a superseded revision marked, and does it remain retrievable?
Which timestamp records the modification event as opposed to receipt of that modification?
Which agent is accountable for this plan and its schedule entries?
Which single role holds write authority over the master copy, and how is that authority transferred?
What evidence records that the plan was approved, by whom and against which revision?
Under what conditions may write or approval authority be delegated, and is the delegation recorded on the plan?
What end state or objective does the plan intend to bring about?
By which measurable criterion is the goal judged achieved rather than merely attempted?
How does the goal decompose into sub-goals and planned actions?
What happens when two goals in the same plan cannot both be satisfied?
Which action type and target object does the planned action denote?
Which conditions must hold for the planned action to be executable?
Which state changes does the planned action expect to produce?
Is the action instantaneous or durative, and are its conditions checked at start, throughout, or at end?
Which lifecycle states may a planned action occupy before it is realized?
Which external condition does the plan take for granted without controlling it?
Who is accountable for monitoring each assumption, and on what cadence?
Which observable signal invalidates the assumption, and what re-planning does it trigger?
How much of the plan fails if this assumption fails?
Which duration estimates carry a distribution rather than a single deterministic value?
Has a schedule risk analysis been run, against which plan revision, and at what confidence level is the committed date set?
Where is schedule reserve held, and who may authorize consuming it?
Which activities drive the greatest schedule risk?
Is the entry anchored as an instant, a start plus duration, a start plus end, or a deadline only?
In which serialization profile and precision are the entry's absolute times expressed?
Is the entry a date-only all-day binding or a time-of-day binding?
Where is the entry expected to take place, and does that place determine its local time?
Is the entry stored as UTC, as local time with a named zone, or as floating local time?
Which time zone database release was in force when the entry was created, and is that release recorded?
What happens to a future entry when its zone's offset or daylight-saving rule changes?
If a stored offset disagrees with the named zone, which one governs?
Does the stated duration mean elapsed time, working time, or resource effort?
Which working calendar, including non-working days and shift hours, applies to this entry?
In which units are durations expressed, and how are partial units rounded?
Which calendar governs when the resource calendar and the activity calendar disagree?
In which recurrence grammar is the pattern expressed, and is it losslessly convertible to the others in use?
Which frequency, interval, by-part and termination terms define the pattern?
Which start value anchors expansion, and in which zone is expansion performed?
Is the series bounded by count, by an end date, or unbounded, and how far should a consumer expand it?
How is a single occurrence identified independently of the series it belongs to?
Does a change apply to one occurrence only or to that occurrence and all later ones?
How are cancelled or excluded occurrences recorded so that expansion does not regenerate them?
When the series rule changes, what becomes of previously detached overrides?
Which ordering relation holds between predecessor and successor: finish-to-start, start-to-start, finish-to-finish or start-to-finish?
What lag or lead applies, in which duration kind, and what justifies it?
What physical or contractual reason justifies the dependency rather than mere convenience?
Which dependencies cross the plan boundary to another party's plan?
Which date constraint is imposed on this entry, and who imposed it?
How flexible is the entry: fixed, movable within a window, or freely schedulable?
When a hard constraint conflicts with network logic, which is honoured and how is the conflict surfaced?
Is the deadline self-imposed, contractual or regulatory?
Does the schedule capture every activity needed to meet the objective, including work performed by other parties?
Which activities have missing predecessors or successors, negative lag, or excessive use of hard constraints?
Can the schedule be traced horizontally across dependent activities and vertically to its summary levels?
Which health metrics are computed, at what thresholds, and against which scheduling run?
Which dates are asserted inputs and which are computed outputs of a scheduling run?
Which continuous path of activities determines the finish date, and how was its validity checked?
What total float and free float does each activity carry, and what threshold counts as unreasonable?
What triggers recomputation, and is the previous computed result retained?
Which agent or resource is assigned to the planned action, in which role and at what allocation?
What availability calendar limits the assigned resource?
Where is the same resource committed to overlapping entries, and how is that resolved?
Which activities carry a duration but no assigned resource, and is that deliberate?
Which party issues the commitment and which party is its beneficiary?
What exactly is promised, by when, and under which qualifying conditions?
Is the commitment informal, contractual or regulatory, and what evidence establishes it?
Who is entitled to verify the commitment's existence and terms?
Which additional duty is triggered when the commitment is not fulfilled?
Which observable event constitutes non-fulfilment, and at what moment is it evaluated?
How is a commitment released, renegotiated or transferred, and whose consent is required?
What evidence closes the commitment as honoured?
In which role does each participant appear on the entry?
What is each participant's current response state, and when was it last updated?
Is a reply expected from this participant, and by when?
When a participant delegates, how are delegator and delegate linked on the entry?
Does this entry consume the participant's availability or leave them free?
How are overlapping commitments detected across separate calendars and plans?
How is an alternative time proposed, accepted or declined?
When an entry moves, what records the previous time and the reason?
Which elements are frozen in the baseline and which remain live?
Who approved the baseline, and under what rule may the plan be re-baselined?
How are multiple concurrent baselines distinguished, and which is current?
How is it proven that a stored baseline has not been altered since freezing?
At what granularity is a change recorded: whole plan, entry, or individual field?
Which controlled reason code explains the change, distinguishing correction of an error from genuine re-planning?
Who authorized the change, and was downstream notification required?
Which timestamps record when the change was decided, applied and observed by consumers?
How is progress expressed, and is the measurement method declared rather than assumed?
Which actual start and finish dates are recorded, and are dates later than the status date rejected?
What variance against the baseline is computed, and at which level of the plan?
As of which status date is the progress statement valid, and who asserted it?
Which recorded acts realize this planned action, and is the correspondence one-to-one?
How is partial or substituted fulfilment represented without overwriting the original intention?
How is this plan recorded as the plan an executing agent actually followed?
How are acts that occurred with no corresponding intention represented?
Which terminal states may a plan reach, and how are they distinguished from one another?
What reason and authority are recorded when a plan is dropped before completion?
What happens to open commitments and future occurrences when the plan closes?
May a closed plan be edited, and if not, how are subsequent corrections expressed?
Which agent, human or software, generated this plan version, and under which activity?
From which prior plan, template or forecast is this plan derived?
Is the planning agent autonomous software, and are its identity and version recorded?
Which upstream instruction or request caused the plan to be created?
At which level of detail is the entry shared: full content, busy-only, or hidden entirely?
Which grants let a non-owner read or write the plan, and do they apply per entry or per plan?
How long are plan, schedule and commitment records retained after closure, and under whose records schedule?
When an entry is deleted, what marker remains so that replicas do not resurrect it?
Which fields may reveal sensitive location, health or negotiation information and must be redacted in projections?
To which external vocabularies does this model map, and which elements are lossy in each direction?
Does an export and re-import round trip preserve identity, revision counter and occurrence overrides?
What evidence supports a conformance claim, as distinct from a mere alignment?
How are locally required fields carried without breaking a receiving implementation?

grok_only.name: What is the authoritative master-system identifier of this plan, and which governed IRI or Dimension ULID is used when the master system is absent or federated?
Is the same UID or uid reused across systems to mean the same plan, and is it large enough to persist at least 255 octets without truncation inside a UTF-8 sequence?
What title, locale and product identifier should agents use when referring to this plan in human and machine interchange?
Which lifecycle status does this plan currently hold, and which aligned vocabulary supplied that code?
Is this intention a proposal, a plan the agent currently holds, a binding order, or an option in a larger plan?
If the plan or planned item reports progress toward completion, what percent-complete or completed flag is asserted, and is that a statement of intention status rather than a recorded act?
Which planned steps does this plan contain, and is any step itself a nested plan?
What intended verb, target, priority and estimated duration describe this planned step?
Which planned input and output variables must exist for this step to be executable as intended, and which standing process definition if any does the step instantiate?
Which recorded acts, if any, are asserted to correspond to this planned step, without storing those acts in this model?
What conditions does this plan rely on, and is each an assumption, precondition, exclusion or do-not-perform instruction?
How sensitive is the plan to this assumption being false, and what signal is monitored to detect that?
Does this assumption reference a condition, observation or other sibling-model entity that lives outside the plan?
Which agent commits, which agent or party is the beneficiary, and which planned item is bound?
What is the current participation or honouring status of this commitment, and is a reply still expected?
What terms, role and penalty or remedy make this intention binding, as distinct from a mere personal plan?
Has participation been delegated, and if so to whom and with what SENT-BY or acting-on-behalf agent remaining responsible?
When is this planned item intended to start and end or fall due, in local civil time and as a UTC instant, and is duration used instead of an explicit end?
Is the binding floating (no time zone), zoned, or show-without-time, and how should free-busy treat that interval?
Where is the occurrence intended to take place, including distinct start and end locations when travel crosses zones?
What is the intended event time versus the created, updated or DTSTAMP observation or ingestion time of this entry?
What frequency, interval, by-parts, until or count, rscale and skip behaviour generate this recurrence set?
Which dates are excluded or additionally included, and which occurrence overrides patch individual instances?
For a materialised occurrence, what recurrence identifier combined with the master UID identifies that instance, and is this a this-and-future split rather than a single-instance override?
Which expansion profile (iCalendar RRULE, JSCalendar recurrenceRules, or a named engine) is authoritative, given known ambiguities in RFC 5545 expansion?
Which time zone or temporal reference system interprets this local time, and which offset applies if the local time falls in a DST discontinuity?
Over which horizon may a consumer read free-busy rather than full entries, and which periods are free, busy, tentative or unavailable?
Does this entry block the calendar (opaque) or leave the interval free for other scheduling (transparent)?
What ordering constraint holds between these planned items, including precedence type and lead or lag gap?
Is this plan or item part of, based on, replacing, parent of or child of another plan, and what grouping REFID if any associates peers?
Independently of project lag, which Allen interval relation holds between the scheduled intervals of the two items?
Does this relationship currently dangle because the target was deleted or cancelled, as RFC 9253 warns for FIRST, NEXT and temporal links?
Who is the Organizer of the master object, and did another user send on that Organizer's behalf?
Which attendees are invited, with what calendar-user type and descriptive role, and are any of them rooms or resources rather than persons?
What calendar address and common name identify this participant, and which person or organization sibling do they reference?
Which scheduling method is being applied, who may send it, and is this a new object or a revision of an existing UID?
What SEQUENCE and stamp time identify this revision, and does it obsolete a previously stored component with the same UID and recurrence id?
If a reply arrives with a lower sequence or earlier stamp than the last persisted attendee response, should it be discarded?
What spoofing, unauthorized organizer-replacement or flood controls apply to this scheduling message, as warned in iTIP security considerations?
Which named baseline freezes this plan, who approved it, and at what freeze time?
Against which baseline should current schedule entries and realized acts be compared, and what planned start, end and duration were frozen?
If a this-and-future change split the series, which UIDs are linked as first and next, and which object was truncated?
Is this snapshot an explicit named baseline, or only an iTIP SEQUENCE increment, and has anyone treated SEQUENCE as if it were an ISO schedule baseline?
Which agent is attributed with this plan version, which activity had this plan, and at what generation time was this version created?
Which prior plan entity is this a revision of, and when was the prior version invalidated as current intention?
Which execution activities correspond to which planned steps, and which steps have no corresponding activity (skipped, failed or not yet started)?
Where a corresponding act exists, what signed difference in start, end or duration is observed relative to the planned entry or baseline, without copying the act into this model?
Which planning agent owns this plan, and which beneficiaries hold verification rights over commitments made to them?
Who may read which projection of this plan (full, agenda, gantt or free-busy), at what classification and through which horizon?
Is this plan or entry cancelled, revoked, entered-in-error, invalidated or actually purged, and must the cancelled record be retained for commitment audit?
What emergency, legal-hold or clinical break-glass exception, if any, overrides the default owner-grant rule, and what audit record is required?

requirements: Resolve every provider-only bundle, layer and finding against primary evidence.
Resolve the model boundary and entry kind before accepting structure.
Verify live URLs and version pins for all accepted sources.
Record every rejected and deferred node with a reason.
Do not publish while any critical conflict remains unresolved.
